newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Wafangdian prices B share IPO at 2.85 yuan.
newsitem.headline: China's Wafangdian prices B share IPO at 2.85 yuan.

text.p: China's largest bearing maker Wafangdian Bearing Co Ltd said on Friday it has priced the initial public offering of its 135 million B shares for listing in Shenzhen at 2.85 yuan, equivalent to HK$2.66 each.
The pricing was announced at an underwriting ceremoney held in Shenzhen on Friday, a company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin newsletter.

The offer gives a price/earnings ratio of 7.9 times based on a 1996 per-share net profit of 0.364 yuan calculated under international accounting standards on a fully diluted basis, the spokesman said.
China Southern Securities Co is the chief domestic underwriter for the offer, which was launched on Friday, he said, adding NatWest Markets Corporate Finance Asia Ltd is the global coordinator.
He did not say when Wafangdian expected to complete the offer and go public.

"The world's largest bearing manufacturer Sweden AB SKF has decided to buy 50 percent of the 130 million B shares, or 65 million shares, at a price equivalent to 3.847 yuan each and promised hold the stock for at least two years," an official said.
SKF will buy the B shares at a price 35 percent higher than public offering price as part of its strategy to enter China's bearing market, the spokesman said.

Wafangdian, which specialises in manufacturing bearings for use in the automobile, railway and petrochemical sectors, plans to use share proceeds to improve production capacity and technology, the official said.

The company, based in Wafangdian city in northeastern Liaoning province, posted net profit of 119 million yuan in 1996, compared with 89.08 million yuan in 1995 and 90.54 million yuan in 1994, under international accounting standards, he said.
He did not issue a profit forecast for 1997.

Before the B share offer, the company had 200 million outstanding state shares, the official said, adding the firm exports 10 percent of its bearings to the United States, southeast Asia and Africa. It sells 90 percent of its products domestically, he said.
